en: The carabao, a large domesticated water buffalo, is the national animal of the Philippines and is traditionally used by farmers to plow rice fields.
Sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower scientifically named Jasminum sambac, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government is the bicameral Congress, which consists of the twenty-four member Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of Luzon over two thousand years ago using ancient stone-wall engineering.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara co-invented the two-way radiotelephone and discovered the physical law of electrical kinetic resistance, now known as the Zara effect.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-backward dance movement mimicking a river's current.
Filipino, which is primarily based on Tagalog, is the national language of the Philippines and is written using the modern twenty-eight letter alphabet.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polymath who wrote the influential novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, every citizen who is at least eighteen years old and registered has the right and duty to vote.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes larger than its brain.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is famously demonstrated when community members physically carry a nipa hut to help a family relocate.
